lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Crestline Logistics appears above the more recent Harbor Payments role, making the section harder to follow.

items.says: The Coastal Marine Services entry distracts from the product-management direction in its current form.
items.because: Its two detailed mechanic bullets may draw attention away from more relevant product work.

items.says: The hydraulic-winch maintenance bullet gives no result.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the work improved reliability or helped meet inspection requirements.

items.says: The carrier-scorecard work gives no result for the business or regional managers.
items.because: The bullet does not show what decision or operational outcome the scorecards informed.

items.says: “Owned” frames the work as a responsibility rather than specific actions.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what you did to produce the scorecards or run the meeting.

items.says: The 30% reduction has no stated baseline or comparison period.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the reduction is measured against.

items.says: The driver-hour savings are buried after a long list of responsibilities.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the clearest evidence of value.

items.says: “Taking over vendor negotiations” is conversational and obscures the specific work.
items.because: The phrase does not clearly name the action you took.

items.says: The dispute-roadmap bullet does not identify the priority selected.
items.because: Readers see prioritization work without knowing what changed on the roadmap.

items.says: The roadmap-priority bullet does not identify the priority selected.
items.because: Readers see that a priority was set without knowing what changed on the roadmap.

items.says: The loss-sizing analysis gives no estimate or comparison between segments.
items.because: Readers cannot judge the scale of the opportunity or why one segment warranted attention.

items.says: The bullet repeats the checkout test and conversion result already reported in the preceding bullet.
items.because: Both bullets describe the test and lift without showing a distinct contribution.

items.says: The claim that the app prevented 9 tonnes of food from being discarded lacks evidence of that counterfactual.
items.because: Redistribution shows that food was picked up, not what would have happened without the app.

items.says: The launch bullet does not show your personal contribution to getting the app live.
items.because: Your role in delivering the launch is unclear.

items.says: The increase is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The rise of 750 users is 187.5% of the starting value of 400.

items.says: “A 150% increase” repeats the growth shown by the before-and-after figures.
items.because: Readers can calculate the change from 400 to 1,150.

items.says: The line attributes the increase in weekly active users to reminders without evidence of a causal link.
items.because: Interviews can inform a feature choice but do not establish that reminders caused usage to rise.

items.says: The finding that led from user interviews to pickup reminders is missing.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what users said that made reminders the right response.

items.says: The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: Relative to the original 75% rate, the increase is about 26.7%.

items.says: The shift-system method does not say what changed about staffing pickup slots.
items.because: A scheduling or coverage detail would make your contribution more evident.

items.says: “By setting up a volunteer shift system” is wordier than a direct action verb.
items.because: A tighter verb would make the contribution easier to scan.

items.says: The client’s approval of a scheduling pilot is repeated in another practicum bullet.
items.because: The two bullets give the same outcome rather than one account linking the savings estimate to approval.

items.says: The intake-form change has no measure of its scale or effect.
items.because: Readers cannot tell how much the form was shortened or whether intake improved beyond staff adoption.

items.says: Passive wording obscures your actions on patient intake and the form.
items.because: Your contribution is hard to distinguish from the team’s outcome.

items.says: The client’s approval of a scheduling pilot is repeated in another practicum bullet.
items.because: The two bullets give the same outcome rather than one account linking the savings estimate to approval.
